newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Two Russian journalists kidnapped in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Two Russian journalists kidnapped in Chechnya.

text.p: Two Russian journalists were kidnapped in broad daylight on Wednesday in the centre of the Chechen capital Grozny, Russian news agencies reported.
Itar-Tass news agency said the journalists worked for the Vzglyad (View) programme, produced by the independent VID production company. The company declined comment.

Tass said the journalists, a reporter and a cameraman, had been seized by unidentified masked men at around 2 p.m. (1000 GMT). They were waiting by their car when two other cars arrived with the kidnappers who fired into the air and then made off with their hostages.

Kidnapping and other crimes are common in rebel Chechnya, where most men are still armed after the region's 21-month war with Russian troops and where jobs are scarce in an economy wrecked by the conflict.
Tens of thousands of people died in the fighting which ended last August.
Last Friday, four Russian journalists were released after three months of captivity in Chechnya.
A television crew of three from NTV commercial television is still being held, though Chechen leader Aslan Maskhadov is personally heading efforts to free them.
Dozens, if not hundreds, of people of other professions are still missing in Chechnya but the Russia media have give a much higher profile to their kidnapped colleagues.

Vzglyad, a weekly current affairs programme on the ORT state channel, recently aired an interview with a Chechen who said he belonged to a gang trying to make money from kidnapping journalists. Officials deny they have paid ransoms to secure the release of those freed earlier.
